correctness.rationale: RESULT.md lines 5–29 and 31–70 count labelled periodic configurations, not basin sizes or orbits. For even n the opposite-shore update maps onto the two constants and the middle layer, complements only the middle layer, and squares to the identity there. The product-and-swap map therefore has Q=s_m, P=s_m², C=(P−Q)/2 and F³=F. In the odd case the diagonal self-spin implements tie retention with nonzero fields; the symmetric cross-time energy strictly increases until a second iterate repeats. Noncentral periodic weights force the four corners. At the two equal central weights, fixedness requires disjointness or covering respectively, with (m+1) choices for the second support after choosing the first at weight m or taking complements. For mixed weights, intersection 0 is fixed, intersection 1 maps to a complementary fixed pair, and intersection ≥2 leaves both central layers. The resulting two fixed corners, 2(m+2) binomial(2m+1,m) central fixed states, and opposing-shore two-cycle give the claimed odd counts including n=3. Stirling gives both recurrent fractions. The packaged code and capture were inspected, not executed. A separate functional-graph enumeration at n=3 through 7 matched all counts and the even one-update result; replay: python3 /workspace/branches/independent_discrete_checks.py. The symbolic argument, not enumeration, proves the all-n claims.
